artifacts.notes: All 676 canvases and exact default 1000-pixel-wide JPEG deliveries in the complete Bonn IIIF manifest are retained in provider order. No missing or failed canvas IDs. The provider sequence includes covers, blanks, two separately paginated parts, errata and the colophon. This establishes completeness of the offered digital sequence, not physical completeness of the historical volume or a complete transcription. Direct image inspections include title and incense openings, part II pp. 3, 86–87, 110–111, 212 and 317, and colophon. Blue reader annotations at part II pp. 110–111 are not evidence of the original printed wording. No OCR is included. Project-assembled ZIP_STORED archive preserves each exact image file plus the exact provider manifest and a hash-bearing sequence map; not a provider-issued ZIP. Bonn’s catalogue extent is 288, 479 pages; this is not reconciled with the 676-image sequence. Part I printed p. 288 is artifact 293, errata begin at 667 and the colophon is 672. No correction of the library’s extent or certification of the physical copy is inferred.

artifacts.notes: Complete Arabic Creed in Tuki’s 1736 Coptic-Arabic Catholic printing, 139 whitespace-separated words after the declared normalization. The parallel Coptic text, surrounding rubrics and the remainder of the service are outside this component. This text records the printed procession clause from the Father and the Son; it does not reconstruct Tuki’s manuscript exemplar or establish the first historical insertion. The whole offered Bonn sequence is retained, but the 676-image sequence does not reconcile with Bonn’s catalogue extent of 288, 479 pages. No whole physical volume or whole text completeness is claimed.

passages.notes: Two AI readers independently inspected and enlarged the retained original page images on 2026-10-17, checking all lexical words and the component boundaries. No unresolved lexical reading remained. This is not a glyph-diplomatic transcription or human specialist certification. The five errata leaves (artifact pages 667–671) were inspected; no listed correction to these Arabic Creed words was identified. The Arabic Creed is read as printed, without importing the Coptic errata or later recensions. Join source line wraps and ten typographic paragraphs into one reading line; omit decorative endpoint rosettes, vowel/accent signs, typographic elongation and discretionary spacing. Do not insert punctuation or modern hamzas. Preserve historical words and spellings, including بالاه, الاه, نومن, وتانس, تالم, العذرى, بلاطس, الاحيا, انقضا and شى. Separate لا يرى as two lexical words. Source terminal yāʾ is historically undotted or not consistently distinguishable at the retained resolution: lexical Unicode ي/ى choices are an explicit reading normalization, not a claim to reproduce printed dotting. Omit the catchwords نحن at the foot of II.85 and مع at the foot of II.86, retaining each only in its following body line. Encode one NFC UTF-8 line with one final LF.
